verdict.rationale: Dagster's docs show `dg dev` starting a local webserver for the project, and a Dagster team member says the design goals included a seamless laptop-to-prod experience and testability by separating business logic from environmental concerns. However, no first-party documentation shows swapping a production destination for a lightweight local one; DuckDB appears only as one user's stack choice. Missing for 10: documented mechanism for pointing pipelines at a lightweight or local destination, first-party docs on local pipeline testing before production, hands-on corroboration of a local-to-prod workflow.

support.subject: As a data engineer, I run and test a pipeline locally against a lightweight destination before it touches production

citations.quote: you can run `dg dev` to start the webserver and navigate to the `Docs` tab for your project's code location

goals were local development (seamless laptop-to-prod dev experience), managing complexity of hundreds of DAGs/thousands of tasks, and testability by separating business logic from environmental concerns
